transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

My family keeps telling me everything is normal, but I’m absolutely convinced they’re secretly working together behind my back. I just can’t shake this belief, no matter what kind of proof or papers they try to show me to convince me otherwise.

Have you experienced any significant changes in your behavior or emotional state, such as becoming easily irritated, anxious, or detached from reality, in addition to these persistent thoughts about your family?

I do get very tense and argumentative whenever I have to interact with my family, and I've started avoiding family gatherings altogether because of it. However, outside of my family, I am functioning completely normally—I still run my office team successfully and do my volunteer shifts without any issues at all. I don't feel detached from reality, just deeply concerned about what they are planning behind my back.
Can you tell me how long you've held this belief about your family, and has it evolved over time into a more complex or detailed theory, or has it remained relatively consistent?

This has been going on for about eleven months now, starting right when we began having issues with selling my parents' house and sorting out their papers. The core belief that my ex-husband and kids are working to cut me out has stayed the same, but it has definitely hardened over time. Now, even minor delays in signing forms or small disagreements just feel like more proof of their plot.

Have you ever experienced any episodes where your belief about your family's plot seemed to momentarily fade or weaken, only to return later, or has it been consistently present and unshakeable since it started?

No, it has never faded or weakened; it has been completely constant and unshakeable for the entire eleven months. Even when they show me emails or legal documents to prove they aren't hiding anything, I just see those papers as part of their cover-up. I have never doubted for a second that they are working against me.
Have you noticed any other delusional beliefs or ideas outside of your family, such as concerns about being followed, poisoned, or having special powers?

No, absolutely not, my mind is completely clear and I don't experience any strange things like being followed or poisoned. My concerns are strictly about my ex-husband, the kids, and their lawyer trying to cut me out of my parents' house. Outside of this family mess, I manage my office team and volunteer shifts completely normally.
Have you ever taken any actions based on your belief that your family is plotting against you, such as hiring a private investigator, confronting them directly, or taking legal action?

Yes, I have confronted them directly about it, which always leads to tense arguments where I try to get them to just admit what they're doing. It has really strained our relationship, but I haven't taken any extreme steps like hiring an investigator or filing lawsuits.
Have you experienced any hallucinations, such as hearing voices that others don't hear, in addition to your delusional beliefs about your family's plot?
No, I've never experienced anything like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there, and my senses are completely normal.
Can you describe any specific behaviors or actions your family members have exhibited that you believe are evidence of their plot against you, and how you interpret these actions?

Whenever there are minor disagreements or delays in signing the legal paperwork for my parents' house in Mexico, I know it is a deliberate stall tactic. Even the emails and documents they show me are just a front; my ex-husband, the kids, and their lawyer are only pretending to include me while secretly plotting to cut me out of all family decisions.
Have you ever considered the possibility, even for a moment, that your family might not be plotting against you, or is this belief something you're absolutely certain about all the time?

No, I am absolutely certain all the time and have never doubted it for a single second. All of their explanations and the documents they show me are clearly just a cover-up to hide what they are actually planning. I know my family, and it is completely obvious to me that they are working behind my back.
Have you noticed any changes in your daily life or routines that are specifically influenced by your belief about your family's plot, aside from avoiding family gatherings?

Outside of family matters, my daily routines are completely unaffected; I still manage my office team and do my volunteer shifts at the senior center without any issues. However, whenever a routine task or conversation involves my ex-husband or my children, I get so focused on their plotting that the interaction becomes incredibly tense, argumentative, and exhausting.
Can you tell me more about what you think is the ultimate goal of your family's supposed plot against you, and what do you believe they hope to achieve by cutting you out?

I am convinced their ultimate goal is to completely undermine my influence and push me out of any decisions regarding my parents' house and family belongings. They want to control the estate and hide their real legal plans from me, using those papers and emails just to keep me quiet. It is incredibly exhausting to know they are doing this just to take away my say in my own family's legacy.
Have you ever experienced any periods where you felt your belief about your family's plot was less intense or you were less preoccupied with it, even if it didn't completely go away?

No, I haven't had any periods where it felt less intense or went away. Ever since this started eleven months ago, it has been a constant, unshakeable conviction that they are plotting against me. I am always on edge and preoccupied whenever any family matters come up.

Have you ever considered seeking a second opinion or an independent assessment of the situation with your family's estate and legal matters to help clarify any potential misunderstandings or miscommunications?

I haven't really thought about getting an independent legal assessment or a second opinion. I feel so completely sure about what they are doing that I just didn't think it would make any difference anyway.

Have you ever experienced any periods where your thoughts, feelings, or behaviors were so disorganized or bizarre that you had trouble functioning in your daily life, outside of the issues with your family?

No, I have never experienced any disorganized or bizarre thoughts, and my daily life is completely normal outside of the family conflict. I still run my office team successfully without any complaints from my boss, and I keep up my volunteer shifts at the senior center just like I always have.
